parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A body starts from rest and moves in the positive x direction. The net force also points in the positive x direction but decreases in magnitude as x increases. Does its kinetic energy increase or decrease with x? Explain.

answer.text: It increases, because the force continues to do positive work. The rate of increase per unit distance becomes smaller as the force decreases.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A block of mass M is released from rest at height 6R on a frictionless track. It later reaches point B at height 2R. Taking gravitational potential energy as zero at height zero, determine its gravitational potential energy, kinetic energy and speed at B. Start from conservation of energy.

answer.text: Initial total energy is 6MgR. At B, Ug = 2MgR, so K = 4MgR. From ½Mv² = 4MgR, v = √(8gR).

fep-48711ac5ebc72e6f-q13:whole.text: A. The tension is perpendicular to the instantaneous displacement, so W = F s cos 90° = 0. It changes the direction of the velocity without changing the kinetic energy.

fep-59e9fdff25044e14-q12:whole.text: D. Useful lifting work = weight × height = 1.5 × 10³ × 10 = 1.5 × 10⁴ J. The supplied energy is useful work/efficiency = (1.5 × 10⁴)/0.20 = 7.5 × 10⁴ J.
fep-59e9fdff25044e14-q12:whole.display_text:
A machine of efficiency 20% raises an object of weight 1.5 × 10³ N through a vertical height of 10 m. What is the total energy supplied to the machine?

A. 3.0 × 10³ J
B. 1.2 × 10⁴ J
C. 1.8 × 10⁴ J
D. 7.5 × 10⁴ J
fep-59e9fdff25044e14-q12:whole.correction: Original asks for work done raising the object but omits the useful-work value from the options. Clarified that the requested quantity is input energy; quantities and choices preserved.
